banff.overview: Glacier-carved valleys and jagged peaks surround trails for every level, with a gondola to the alpine meadows at Sunshine. Multi-day routes like the 27-mile, 3-day Skyline Trail cross high passes, while day hikes range from easy lakeshore paths to strenuous climbs. In July and August the parks are crowded, especially at Moraine Lake, Lake Louise and Johnston Canyon, where parking fills early, so Moraine Lake and Lake Louise now need shuttle reservations. The best conditions run from late June to September.

months.9: Cooler temperatures and golden larches make for excellent hiking. The color lasts only two to three weeks, so Larch Valley, the most popular larch hike and reached from Moraine Lake, is extremely busy in the second half of the month, and early snowstorms can briefly close the highest passes.

nepal.overview: Some of the world's most legendary hiking journeys are in the Himalayas of Nepal, where multi-day tea-house routes like the Everest Base Camp trek (about 80 miles over 12 to 14 days) and the Annapurna Circuit (about 100 miles over 13 to 20 days, over the 17,769-foot Thorung La) deliver views of the highest peaks on Earth. Many trailheads are reached by small mountain flights. Views are clearest in October and November; spring brings afternoon haze but blooming rhododendron forests, and the monsoon clouds the mountains from June to August.

months.3: Spring trekking conditions emerge as the snow line retreats and high passes become accessible. The lower trails are moderate and lined with the first blooming rhododendrons, with clear mornings, but afternoon haze and cloud often hide distant peaks at lower elevations.
months.4: The spring peak brings excellent conditions across the high routes, with massive rhododendron forests blooming in red, pink, and white along the moderate lower trails. Mornings offer sharp mountain views before afternoon haze and cloud build, and views stay clearer above about 13,000 feet.
months.5: Heat builds in the lower valleys and haze and pre-monsoon clouds often obscure the peaks by midday, making early starts essential. The high-altitude routes remain open and strenuous, but the window for clear panoramas narrows.

swissalps.overview: Trails run beneath the Matterhorn and the surrounding glaciers. The Gornergrat railway, which climbs to 10,135 feet, and a network of cable cars lift hikers to high alpine trails, so a day hike can start far above the valley. The 130-mile Walker's Haute Route from Chamonix to Zermatt is a trek of 12 to 14 days, crossing high passes and valleys. The main hiking season runs from late June to September, when the high trails are clear of snow.

torres-del-paine.overview: Granite towers, glaciers and turquoise lakes surround the trails here. Day hikes start from trailheads reached by bus or catamaran, while the famous W Trek (about 40 miles in 4 to 6 days) and O Circuit (about 80 miles in 7 to 9 days) offer strenuous multi-day routes between refugios. The weather is notoriously windy, and the main trekking window runs from October to April when the trails and huts are fully open.
